articles.title: Wife Beats Husband with Slippers After ‘Triple Talaq’ Pronouncement
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Rampur, Uttar Pradesh – A dramatic confrontation outside the Rampur District Court has gone viral after a woman thrashed her husband with slippers moments after he allegedly pronounced triple talaq. Asiya, a resident of Bambura village, married Ashid Ali of Dheemri village in 2018.

body.html:
Rampur, Uttar Pradesh – A dramatic confrontation outside the Rampur District Court has gone viral after a woman thrashed her husband with slippers moments after he allegedly pronounced triple talaq.

Asiya, a resident of Bambura village, married Ashid Ali of Dheemri village in 2018. The couple has two daughters, aged six and two. Asiya has accused her husband and in-laws of dowry harassment, domestic violence, and of throwing her out after childbirth. Five months ago, she filed a maintenance case and began living at her maternal home. She further alleges that her husband forcibly took away her daughters during the dispute.

On Friday, after attending a family court hearing with her maternal aunt, Asiya claims her husband and father-in-law followed her outside, hurled abuses, and pressured her to withdraw her case. She alleges that, instigated by his father, Ashid Ali pronounced triple talaq three times and then assaulted her.

In retaliation, Asiya attacked him with slippers, landing five strikes in five seconds, grabbed his collar, and tore his kurta. Onlookers recorded the scuffle, which quickly spread across social media.

Asiya has submitted a complaint to the Superintendent of Police demanding an FIR against her husband and father-in-law. Meanwhile, no police complaint or detailed defense has been reported from the husband’s side.

The viral video has ignited public debate over triple talaq, domestic abuse, and women’s right to resist alleged provocation.

articles.title: Woman Smokes Inside AC Train Coach, Argues With Passengers — Breaks Down When TC Confronts Her
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: New Delhi: A video going viral on social media shows a woman smoking a cigarette inside the air-conditioned coach of a passenger train, leading to heated arguments with fellow travellers. In the clip, a male passenger confronts her, saying smoking is prohibited.

body.html:
New Delhi: A video going viral on social media shows a woman smoking a cigarette inside the air-conditioned coach of a passenger train, leading to heated arguments with fellow travellers.

In the clip, a male passenger confronts her, saying smoking is prohibited. When he begins recording, the woman reacts angrily: “You are making a video, this is very wrong. Delete it immediately.” She further argues, “I am not spending your money to smoke. This is not your train. Go call the police.”

Another co-passenger can be heard saying: “This is an AC compartment. Don’t you know smoking is not allowed here?”

When the matter escalated, a ticket checker (TC) intervened. He informed the woman that smoking inside trains is illegal and presented three options: pay a fine, be let off with a warning, or face police action. At this stage, the woman reportedly panicked and broke down in tears.

Indian Railways officials said the case has been forwarded to concerned authorities for further action. However, the authenticity and details of the viral video could not be independently verified.

articles.title: Agra Blind Murder Case Solved: Nephew Killed, Burnt Over Blackmail Threats
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Agra (UP): In a chilling revelation, Agra Police have cracked a blind murder case from February 18, 2024, exposing a brutal conspiracy driven by blackmail.

body.html:
Agra (UP): In a chilling revelation, Agra Police have cracked a blind murder case from February 18, 2024, exposing a brutal conspiracy driven by blackmail.

The victim, Rakesh (son of Lal Singh), was lured to a sweet shop by his uncle Devi Ram (son of Shankar Singh Baghel, resident of Kuboolpur, PS Malpura) and strangled to death. The accused, along with his nephew Nitya Kishore (absconding), stuffed the body into a plastic drum, transported it by loader to a deserted area near the Khari river, and set it ablaze with petrol in an attempt to erase evidence.

🔎 Motive: Blackmail over daughter’s photos

Police investigations revealed that Rakesh was allegedly in contact with the minor daughter of accused Devi Ram. He had secretly taken her photos while bathing and later began blackmailing the family. Enraged, Devi Ram decided to eliminate him.

🕵️ The Cover-Up
● Murder weapon: muffler & iron wire
● Body burnt inside a drum
● Mobile phone, muffler, and wire dumped in the Khari river
● Motorcycle abandoned on the highway
● Accused fled to Delhi, shutting his shop to avoid suspicion

On February 20, 2024, police recovered a half-burnt body near the river. Initial identification failed, and the body was confirmed as Rakesh only after DNA testing, which matched with his mother.

🚨 Breakthrough & Arrest
After months of surveillance and technical tracking, a joint team of Malpura Police, SOG, and Surveillance Cell arrested Devi Ram on September 15, 2025, near Jagdishpur bridge. During interrogation, he confessed to the murder. His accomplice, Nitya Kishore, remains absconding.

Police confirmed further efforts are underway to trace and arrest the co-accused.

articles.title: Bidar Horror: Stepmother Pushes 7-Year-Old to Death from 3rd Floor
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bidar (Karnataka): A shocking case of cruelty has emerged from Adarsh Colony, Bidar city, where a 7-year-old girl was allegedly murdered by her stepmother, who pushed her from the terrace of a third-floor building.

body.html:
Bidar (Karnataka): A shocking case of cruelty has emerged from Adarsh Colony, Bidar city, where a 7-year-old girl was allegedly murdered by her stepmother, who pushed her from the terrace of a third-floor building.

The victim, Saanvi, was taken upstairs on August 27 by her stepmother Radha under the pretext of playing a game. Once on the terrace, Radha allegedly pushed the child to her death. Initially, the incident was dismissed as an accident, and Saanvi’s father Siddhant lodged an accidental death complaint the following day.

CCTV footage reveals truth

On September 12, a neighbor shared CCTV footage showing Radha’s suspicious movements with the child before her death. Following this, Saanvi’s grandmother lodged a fresh complaint at Gandhiganj police station.

Police investigation revealed that Saanvi’s biological mother had died six years ago, after which Siddhant remarried Radha in 2023. The couple has twin children. Radha reportedly confessed to killing Saanvi due to disputes over property division.

Arrest and custody
Radha has been arrested and remanded to judicial custody. Police confirmed she admitted to the crime during interrogation.

articles.title: NEET Aspirant (19) Brutally Killed by Cattle Smugglers, Head Crushed — Mob Burns Vehicle
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Gorakhpur (U.P.): A shocking case has emerged from Maua Chaapi village in Pipraich, where a 19-year-old NEET aspirant was brutally murdered by cattle smugglers on Monday night.

body.html:
Gorakhpur (U.P.): A shocking case has emerged from Maua Chaapi village in Pipraich, where a 19-year-old NEET aspirant was brutally murdered by cattle smugglers on Monday night.

According to police, around 10–15 smugglers in three vehicles reached the student’s warehouse around 11:30 pm to loot cattle. On being alerted by his cousin, the student rushed to the spot on a scooter along with nearly a dozen villagers.

The group confronted the smugglers, who then overpowered the student, forced him into a DCM vehicle and killed him. His body, with the head crushed, was found nearly 4 km away from his house after 4.5 hours of frantic searching by family members.

Following the murder, enraged locals caught one smuggler, beat him brutally and set his vehicle on fire. When police intervened, clashes broke out; SP North Jitendra Srivastava and Pipraich SHO were injured in the scuffle. The injured smuggler was later admitted to hospital.

Police recovered 2–3 cattle from the smugglers’ pickup. On Tuesday morning, villagers staged a road blockade on the Gorakhpur–Pipraich road, demanding justice. Heavy police deployment, including forces from four stations and PAC, has been stationed at the site, with senior officials trying to pacify the agitated family and villagers.

articles.title: Hyderabad Flood Horror: Retaining Wall Collapse Sweeps Away Youngster in Parsigutta
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Hyderabad: Heavy rains lashed the city last night, leading to the collapse of a nala retaining wall at Parsigutta in Musheerabad. The incident caused severe flooding in nearby bastis, with water gushing into several houses and resulting in extensive property loss.

body.html:
Hyderabad: Heavy rains lashed the city last night, leading to the collapse of a nala retaining wall at Parsigutta in Musheerabad. The incident caused severe flooding in nearby bastis, with water gushing into several houses and resulting in extensive property loss.

According to the HYDRAA Commissioner, all residents were safely rescued, except for a youngster who was tragically washed away in the floodwaters. Officials confirmed that apart from this incident, no further loss of life was reported.

Videos from the site clearly show water from the nala breaching the wall and flooding adjoining residential areas, leaving behind destruction and hardship for local families.

articles.title: Last party celebrated in ICU: Daughter battling cancer
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Udaipur/Jalore – A heart-wrenching story has emerged from Rajasthan, where 27-year-old Priyanka alias Pihu, battling a rare bone cancer, Ewing Sarcoma, celebrated her “last moments” by cutting a cake inside the ICU—just seven days before her death.

body.html:
Udaipur/Jalore – A heart-wrenching story has emerged from Rajasthan, where 27-year-old Priyanka alias Pihu, battling a rare bone cancer, Ewing Sarcoma, celebrated her “last moments” by cutting a cake inside the ICU—just seven days before her death.

On 25 August, Priyanka’s in-laws and family gathered at Pacific Hospital, Udaipur. Lying on a hospital bed, attached to machines, she suddenly asked her father: “Papa, bring a cake. I want to celebrate my last moments. Write Pihu–Lucky on it.”

Her father, jeweller Narpat Singh of Jalore, broke down as he fulfilled her wish. Priyanka cut the cake with her husband Lakshyaraj Singh, a builder from Raniwada, and fed pieces to everyone, saying: “I want to die laughing.”

On 2 September at 1 pm, Priyanka breathed her last—still smiling. Just 20 minutes before her death, she asked her brother Jaipal to eat food, assuring him she wasn’t “going anywhere.”

Priyanka, the third among four siblings, was bright in studies—BBA graduate and CA Inter qualified. She was married in January 2023, but soon after, leg pain led to the devastating diagnosis. Despite three spine surgeries and radiation, doctors gave up hope by August 2025.

Her father recalls: “That day even the doctors and hospital staff cried. My daughter wanted to leave this world with a smile, and she did. She has taught us how to live.”
